findings.evidence: Feature body rules restate triage a model already applies: "NEEDS_REVIEW is any logic or behavior change; APPROVED is only trivial non-logic change (comment typos, formatting, private renames). When in doubt, NEEDS_REVIEW." The record's s008 row covers only the trimmed enumeration, not this surviving restatement.
findings.fix: Keep the two labels and the signature/public-behavior note the template depends on; move the definitions of what counts as logic to skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md next to the changeset template and record the move. Do not delete the labels.

findings.evidence: Section 3 is a process workflow, but the same decision is stated again in 1.6, 1.7, phase 2 and phase 3 (push ordering, missing-script stop, lookup truncation), so the procedure is not one sequence an agent can follow without reconciling copies.
findings.fix: Keep phases 1-6 as the only ordered procedure and leave sections 1-2 as the rules those phases cite, deleting the repeated command sequences from the phase text and recording each removed duplicate.

findings.evidence: The squash/rebase gotcha names the failure ("an older cycle's PRs can be picked as sources") but the hard-learned confirmation is deferred to 2.2, so the Gotchas list itself does not say why the agent must stop.
findings.fix: Add the 2.2 reason to that gotcha: detection assumes merge commits, so when git log --merges does not show every SRC merge the command stops and asks for --reuse-from rather than publishing a possibly stale body.

findings.evidence: The description says what the command does and names triggers ("open, write, refresh or describe a pull request", "promote develop to main", "reuse merged PR bodies") and a boundary, but it never names the accepted flags --diagrams, --reuse-from or --base.
findings.fix: Create or update the GitHub pull request for the current branch from its committed diff: summary, changeset triage, optional Mermaid or draw.io diagram, promotion-branch bodies reused from merged PRs, and reviewers. Use when asked to open, write, refresh or describe a pull request, "explain PR changes", "open or refresh the PR summary", "promote develop to main", or "reuse merged PR bodies", including with --diagrams=none|mermaid|drawio, --reuse-from=<PR> or --base=<branch>. Pushes feature branches and writes PRs. Not for a read-only explanation of a diff (use explain-changes-mental-model).

findings.evidence: The command is 442 lines. Templates, assembly code and the none-mode filter are already loaded from skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, but phase 4 and phase 5 still inline the attach, branch and partial-failure recipes that the same file's "Branch publish and attach recovery" section already holds.
findings.fix: Replace the phase 5 attach/branch/partial-failure command blocks with one conditional read of the "Branch publish and attach recovery" section of skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, keeping only the stop conditions that the phase itself must enforce.

findings.evidence: 2.9 gives a high-freedom diagram-type choice ("flowchart TD, with LR only for a row of at most four nodes") while also requiring a read of authoring-rules.md, whose section 1 says an API call chain is a sequenceDiagram and a flowchart is used only after every other type loses. The two defaults disagree on the same decision.
findings.fix: Make authoring-rules.md section 1 the only type default and keep the inline minimums strictly as the fallback for when neither rules file exists, matching its direction, grouping and classDef rules.

findings.evidence: A mermaid or none feature PR "makes no pr-diagrams.sh call of any kind", but 1.4 says a run with --reuse-from uses PRD and sets REPO from `bash "$PRD" repo`, and phase 3 step 5 runs `bash "$PRD" reviewers` on every reuse path. The no-call branch and the reviewers branch do not resolve to one outcome.
findings.fix: State one rule: a mermaid or none feature PR without --reuse-from makes no script call and parses REPO inline; with --reuse-from it still calls `bash "$PRD" repo` and `reviewers` and stops when the script is missing, as 1.5 already says.
